concept.title: Coldstore
concept.setting: A decommissioned harbor cold-store: a three-room refrigerated warehouse abandoned when the cannery folded, now picked over by scavengers who rarely all walk back out. You enter through the gutting floor, and the only way home is the loading dock on the far side of the freezer.
core_mechanics: Three interconnected rooms in a fixed loop -- gutting floor, freezer core, loading dock -- joined by heavy roller doors that groan when you open them and give away your position.

Randomised loot spawns each run: crates, lockers, and frozen body-caches roll from a weighted table, with the richest gear buried deepest in the freezer core so reward scales with how far you overcommit.

Single extraction trigger at the loading dock -- stand in the marked zone and hold for 8 seconds; the extract chime is audible building-wide, turning the last stretch into the tensest moment of the run.
Limited-slot rig: you carry only what fits, so every pickup forces a drop, and you extract with exactly what's on your back -- die and it all spills.
A single sound-hunting AI scavenger stalks the depot, drawn to gunfire, sprinting footsteps, and the extract chime -- staying quiet is the only real defense.
Permadeath per run seeds the world: loot you die carrying spills into the next run's spawn table, so the depot slowly fills with the ghosts of your failed pulls.
concept.art_style: Tight 32x32 pixel art in a cold, desaturated palette of frost-white, rust brown, and sodium-lamp amber, with heavy dithered shadows and a single flickering light source per room casting long moving silhouettes.
concept.target_mood: Held-breath tension -- the specific dread of being one room too deep with a full rig and a long, loud walk back to the only door.
concept.description: Coldstore distills the extraction-shooter loop -- enter, loot, extract -- down to three rooms and five minutes. Push deeper into a frozen abandoned cold-store for better loot, but every step from the entrance is a step you have to survive on the way back. A lone sound-hunting scavenger, groaning doors, and an 8-second extract timer that the whole building can hear make greed the deadliest thing you carry. Loot lost on death respawns into future runs, so the depot remembers everyone who didn't make it -- including you.
unique_selling_points: A full extraction-shooter run compressed into three rooms and roughly 300 seconds -- the genre stripped to its tensest core for a true micro-prototype.
Your carried loot becomes the next run's loot table: every death re-seeds the depot, so the world visibly accumulates the wreckage of prior attempts.
One sound-driven hunter and a building-wide extract chime turn the final 8 seconds into the scariest decision in the run.

world.name: The Coldstore
world.description: A decommissioned harbor cold-store rendered as a single, brutal extraction loop. Three refrigerated rooms — the gutting floor, the freezer core, and the loading dock — chained in a fixed triangle by heavy roller doors that groan and betray your position. You enter through the gutting floor; the only way home is the extraction zone on the loading dock, on the far side of the freezer. Push deeper for richer loot, then survive the long, loud walk back while a lone sound-hunting scavenger listens for your mistakes.
world.lore_summary: When the cannery folded, the harbor's three-room cold-store was left powered-down and rotting, its compressors ticking as they thawed. Scavengers found the frozen stock and buried gear first, then found each other, and now few who go in for the deep caches walk back out through the loading dock. Something adapted to the dark and the cold and learned that noise means prey — it patrols the roller-door loop, drawn to gunfire, to sprinting boots, and above all to the building-wide chime of an extraction in progress. Everyone who dies in here leaves their rig where they fall, and the frost claims it into the next scavenger's spawn table. The depot remembers every failed pull, including yours.

regions.name: The Coldstore
regions.description: A three-room refrigerated warehouse frozen mid-decay: frost-white rime creeping over rust-brown steel, sodium-lamp amber bleeding from one flickering fixture per room, dithered shadows swinging long across the floor. The rooms form a fixed loop joined by three heavy roller doors, each one a groaning announcement of where you are. There is exactly one way out, and it is the loudest place to stand in the building.

rooms.name: Gutting Floor
rooms.description: Where you come in. Long gutting tables slick with old frost, drainage channels choked with rime, rows of rusted hooks swaying on a chain track that never stopped. One sodium lamp stutters overhead, throwing the hooks' shadows back and forth across the tiles. Loot here is thin and shallow — the picked-over crates and lockers nearest the door — but it is the safest air in the building and the room every run begins and, if you're lucky, ends beside.

rooms.name: Freezer Core
rooms.description: The deep room — the coldest, darkest heart of the loop, where the richest gear is buried in frozen body-caches and sealed cold-crates that the fold left untouched. The single lamp here barely holds, guttering to near-black between pulses, and the silhouettes that swing across the shelving are not always yours. This is where reward scales with how far you overcommit, and where the scavenger hunts most. Every step in is a step you have to carry back out, loud rig and all.

rooms.name: Loading Dock
rooms.description: The far side of the freezer and the only way home. A concrete apron under a half-raised bay door, one painted extraction zone marked on the floor, a dead forklift and stacked pallets for whatever cover they're worth. Stand in the zone and hold for eight seconds — the extract chime rings through every room in the building, and the last stretch to this door becomes the tensest walk of the run. Mid-grade loot sits here too, tempting one more pickup before you commit.

points_of_interest: The painted extraction zone on the loading dock — the single trigger for going home
Frozen body-caches in the freezer core, where dead scavengers' rigs re-seed the loot table
The three groaning roller doors that give away your position every time you open one
The one flickering sodium lamp per room, the only light and the source of every moving silhouette
regions.ambient_mood: held-breath dread — one room too deep with a full rig and a long, loud walk back to the only door

connections.description: The first roller door, off the gutting floor into the freezer core. It groans on its track loud enough to carry building-wide — opening it tells the depot exactly where you are and which way you're headed.
The deep door, out of the freezer core onto the loading dock. Crossing it committed means you have your full rig and only the extraction walk left — the loudest, tensest threshold in the loop.

The service roller door closing the loop back to the gutting floor, letting you circle the depot instead of doubling straight back through the freezer — for the price of one more groaning announcement.

dungeons.name: The Coldstore Loop
dungeons.theme: Abandoned refrigerated harbor warehouse — frost-white and rust, one failing lamp per room, a sound-hunting scavenger, and a single eight-second extraction that the whole building can hear.

rooms.name: Gutting Floor
rooms.description: Run entry. Gutting tables, swinging hooks, and clogged drains under one stuttering sodium lamp. Shallow, picked-over loot and the lowest danger in the loop — the room you spawn beside and the one you pray to reach again with a full back.

rooms.name: Freezer Core
rooms.description: The deep room and the scavenger's favored hunting ground. Frozen body-caches and sealed cold-crates hold the richest gear in the building, guarded by near-total dark between the lamp's dying pulses. Reward scales with how far you overcommit; so does the odds you never leave.

rooms.name: Loading Dock
rooms.description: The extraction point: one painted zone, hold for eight seconds, and a chime that rings through every room. The only way home, and the loudest place to stand in the depot.

connections.description: Roller door from the gutting floor into the freezer core — groans building-wide when opened.
Roller door from the freezer core out onto the loading dock — the committed-and-loaded threshold.
Service roller door closing the loop from the dock back to the gutting floor.

quests.title: The First Walk Back
quests.description: Greta pulls you aside before you touch a crate. Everyone's first run is the same lesson: getting in is free, getting out is the whole game. Grab something worthless, learn the loop, and stand in the painted zone until the chime lets go. If you can survive one loud extraction, you might survive a greedy one later.

objectives.description: Hear Greta out on the gutting floor before you head in.
Pull anything from a shallow crate or locker near the entrance.
Cross the freezer core to the loading dock and find the painted extraction zone.
Stand in the zone and hold through all eight seconds of the chime.

failure_conditions: The player dies anywhere in the loop before the extraction completes

quests.title: The Fence's Cut
quests.description: Marrow doesn't go in anymore — she waits at the bay door and buys what walks out. She'll pay real scrip for sealed cannery stock, the safe pull nobody dies for. Fill three rig slots with frozen tins and bring them to the dock. It's the coward's run, and cowards are the ones still trading.

objectives.description: Loot three sealed Frozen Stock Tins from crates around the loop.
Extract with the tins and hand them to Marrow at the loading dock.

failure_conditions: The player dies carrying the tins, spilling them back into the depot

quests.title: Run Silent
quests.description: Greta's real lesson, the one that kept her breathing: the depot only kills the loud. Make a full loop and extract without ever firing a gun — grease a door, feltsole your boots, throw a can if you must, but never once give the Listener your bearing. Do it clean and she'll trust you with the quiet gear.

objectives.description: Use a Tin of Door Grease to cross at least one roller door without the groan.
Complete an extraction without ever firing the Sidearm or the Scattergun.

failure_conditions: The player fires the Scavenger's Sidearm or the Thawline Scattergun during the run
The Listener detects and reaches the player

quests.title: The Deep Pull
quests.description: Marrow's seen your clean runs and wants the caches only the brave reach. Push all the way into the freezer core, crack a frozen body-cache for rare gear, and carry it back through two doors and the Listener's favorite room. The pay is triple the tins. So is the odds you don't come back.

objectives.description: Enter the freezer core, the deepest room in the loop.
Break open a rare frozen body-cache and take what's inside.
Extract at the loading dock still carrying the rare pull.

failure_conditions: The player dies in the freezer core, spilling the cache into the next run's spawn table

quests.title: The Depot Remembers
quests.description: There's a voice in the freezer core that isn't the wind — Kell, frozen where he fell, still counting the dead by their tags. He'll give you the bundle if you promise to find his rig, the one the frost swallowed into this run's spawns. Wear the Ghost-Rig Tags and the dead point the way to the dead. One day someone wears yours.

objectives.description: Cut the Ghost-Rig Tags free from Kell's frozen body-cache.
Follow the tags to the richest re-seeded body-cache — a prior scavenger's spilled rig.
Carry the recovered ghost-rig out through the extraction zone.

failure_conditions: The player dies carrying the ghost-rig, adding their own tags to Kell's count

quests.title: Silence the Listener
quests.description: Everyone's run ends the same eventually — the thing in the loop hears you and comes. Marrow says there's one gun deep enough to end it: the Thawline Scattergun, sealed in a cold-crate at the core. Take it up, and understand the joke — the only weapon that can kill the Listener is the loudest thing in the building, and firing it calls it straight to you. Win the fight you're forced to start.

objectives.description: Recover the Thawline Scattergun from the sealed cold-crate in the freezer core.
Put the Listener down when the blast draws it to your position.
Extract at the loading dock after the depot goes quiet.

failure_conditions: The player is killed by the Listener before the extraction completes

npcs.name: Greta 'Old Teeth'
npcs.description: The gutting floor's fixture — a veteran scavenger who lost her nerve for the deep room and now sits by the entrance rethreading hooks, warning every newcomer with the same three rules. She's the reason a few of them walk back out. She never goes past the first door anymore, and she won't tell you why.
npcs.appearance: A wiry woman bundled in frost-stiff canvas and a moth-eaten thermal hood, gutting hook worn on a belt loop, half her teeth gone and the rest capped in dull steel. Sodium light catches the rime in her eyebrows; she never fully faces the freezer door.

fears: the sound of a groaning door behind her
quirks: counts to eight under her breath without meaning to
taps the wall twice before she'll open a door
personality.speech_pattern: clipped, low, half-whispered — she talks like the walls are listening

special_abilities: reads the loop's noise level at a glance

relationships.description: They ran the loop together for years until Greta stopped going in. Marrow stayed at the door; Greta stayed at the other.
Kell was her last partner into the core. She hears his voice in there and can't bring herself to answer it.

entries.activity: rethreading hooks and watching the entrance

greeting: New face. Good. Old faces are the ones hanging on the hooks.
Keep your voice down in here. It listens.
idle: One flickering lamp, one groaning door, one thing that hunts. Learn all three or feed all three.
Eight seconds. That's how long the chime holds you still while it comes. Eight.
The stock outlasted the cannery. Most of us don't outlast the stock.
quest_offer: Grab something worthless and get to that door. Prove you can leave before you learn to be greedy.
Run me a clean loop. No guns. Not one. Then we'll talk about what I keep quiet.
quest_complete: You walked back out. Most don't. Don't let it go to your head — greed's the only thing that carries as far as a gunshot.
Silent the whole way. Good. You'll live longer than the loud ones did.
warning: You hear that door groan? Now it knows where you are.
Every step deeper is a step you carry back. Don't forget the walk.

npcs.name: Marrow
npcs.description: The fence at the bay door. She stopped going in the day she watched a partner spill a full rig in the core, and now she trades from the concrete apron — brass scrip for whatever you drag out, gear for whatever you'll owe. She never crosses the extraction line inward. She's watched too many people not come back across it.
npcs.appearance: A broad, still figure in a quilted dock coat, breath fogging under the half-raised bay door, a strongbox of brass tokens at her boots. Amber lamplight pools on a face that gives away nothing; frost has made a beard of her scarf.

fears: the extract chime she can't un-hear
quirks: weighs every tin in her palm before naming a price
won't say the Listener's name, calls it 'the tenant'
personality.speech_pattern: even, unhurried, dry — a fence's cadence that never rises

special_abilities: reads a scavenger's odds by how full their rig is

relationships.description: Two halves of a run that stopped running. Greta guards the way in, Marrow the way out, and neither goes between anymore.
Pallett brings her the best caches and the worst attitude. She pays him and watches him leave.

entries.activity: fencing loot at the bay door

greeting: You crossed the line the right way — outward. What'd you bring me?
Full rig. Good runs and dead men both come in with a full rig. Which are you?
idle: Dead company's money for a dead man's gear. Still spends.
I buy what walks out. I don't ask what didn't.
The tenant's quiet today. Don't make me revise that.
quest_offer: Tins are safe money. Bring me three and we're square.
There's a scattergun in the core that can end the tenant. It's also the loudest way to introduce yourself. Your call.
Push to the deep caches. Triple the pay, triple the reasons you won't spend it.
quest_complete: Clean pull. Here's your cut — count it, I always do.
You brought the rare stuff back across the line. That's rarer than the stuff.
warning: That chime's ringing. Everything in here just heard where you'll be for eight seconds.
Don't fire that thing near my door. I'll take the gear off your corpse either way.

npcs.name: Pallett
npcs.description: A brash younger scavenger who works the same loop you do and wants you to know he works it better. He runs loud and lucky, hauls out caches that should've killed him, and treats the freezer core like a personal shelf. Sooner or later luck runs the same way for everyone in here. He doesn't believe that yet.
npcs.appearance: Lean and twitchy in a patched dock jacket hung with rattling trophies, a felt-wrapped sidearm on his hip he loves too much to keep quiet. Frost on a cocky grin; his boots are loud and he's proud of the stride.

fears: being the one left holding the loud gun
the silence right before the tenant arrives
quirks: whistles when he's nervous, which is loud, which is a problem
personality.speech_pattern: fast, boastful, needling — talks more than is safe in here

special_abilities: draws the hunter's attention off you when he's louder

relationships.description: He brings Marrow the deepest caches and the loudest opinions. She pays for one and endures the other.
He calls Greta 'the doorstop' and ignores every rule she's tried to hand him.

greeting: Oh, it's you. Try to keep up, or don't — more caches for me.
You still counting to eight like the doorstop taught you? Cute.
idle: Deepest crate in the core's got my name on it. Literally, I named it.
Loud gets you the good stuff first. Quiet gets you the leftovers.
The tenant? Never touched me. Never will.
taunt: Bet I clear the core and extract before you grease your first door.
You extract with what's on your back. Mine's fuller. Math's simple.
combat: You're gonna make it hear us both!
warning: ...you hear that? No? Good. Keep not hearing it.
Okay. Okay, that door groaned and it wasn't me. That wasn't me.

npcs.name: Frostbit Kell
npcs.description: A body-cache in the freezer core that still speaks — or seems to, in the space between the lamp's dying pulses. Kell went in with Greta and never came back across, and now he counts the dead by their tags and asks passing scavengers to find the rig the frost took from him. Whether he's a ghost, a hallucination of the cold, or just the depot remembering out loud, the tags he gives are real.
npcs.appearance: A frost-glazed shape half-fused to the shelving, one hand still closed around a wire loop of stamped dog-tags. Rime bridges his eyelashes; an amber glow seems to sit behind the ice when the lamp gutters, and his voice arrives without his mouth moving.

values: the dead pointing the way to the dead
warning the living without scaring them off
fears: being forgotten into the spawn table
the silence after the last scavenger stops coming
quirks: recites names between the lamp's flickers
never speaks while the room is fully lit
personality.speech_pattern: slow, layered, half-echo — like the cold itself doing the talking

relationships.description: He knows she hears him from the gutting floor and can't come in. He doesn't blame her. He just keeps his tags ready.

entries.activity: frozen in the shelving, counting the tags

greeting: Still... warm. You're still warm. Good. Come closer — no, not too loud.
The lamp dips and I can speak. Listen fast.
idle: Everyone who dies in here leaves their rig where they fall. I count them. It's all I do now.
The frost claims it into the next one's table. Yours too, someday. I'll count you kindly.
Carry the tags and the dead point the way to the dead.
quest_offer: Take my tags. Find the rig the cold swallowed this run — the richest one. It was somebody, once.
One of the caches out there is you. A you that didn't make it. The tags will show you. Don't flinch.
quest_complete: You brought it back across the line. One less name only I remember.
The depot remembers everyone. Today it remembered gently, because of you.
warning: It favors this room. It's near. Lower your voice or join my count.
Don't run. Running is a sound. Sound is how it finds the warm ones.

npcs.name: The Listener
npcs.description: The thing that adapted to the dark and the cold and learned that noise means prey. Once a scavenger, maybe — now something that patrols the roller-door loop by ear alone, drawn to gunfire, to sprinting boots, to a groaning door, and above all to the building-wide chime of an extraction in progress. It cannot see well in the sodium dark. It does not need to. Stay silent and it walks past. Make one sound and it walks toward.
npcs.appearance: A long, low silhouette that reads as human only in the wrong light — frost-crusted and rag-wound, head cocked permanently to one side as if always listening. It moves without weight until it sprints, and then the whole loop hears it come. Its eyes are pale and useless; its ears are not.

quirks: freezes utterly at any new sound to fix its bearing
loses the trail completely the instant its prey goes quiet
personality.speech_pattern: wordless — a dragging rasp, a listening stillness, a sudden sprint

special_abilities: sound-hunting: navigates by noise, not sight
drawn to gunfire, sprinting footsteps, groaning doors, and the extract chime
loses all track of silent prey
favors the freezer core, patrols the full loop

entries.activity: patrolling the loop by ear, favoring the deep room

alerted: [a dragging rasp stops — it heard you]
hunting: [it's in the room the chime came from]
lost_track: [the sprint slows — you went quiet in time]
[it stands still, listening for a sound you didn't make]

items.name: Gutting Hook
items.description: A meat hook pried off the swaying chain track on the gutting floor, its point honed on the drainage grate. It kills without a bang — the only weapon in the depot that won't call the scavenger down on you.

effects.name: Silent Work
effects.description: Strikes make no report and add nothing to the depot's noise level — a clean kill leaves the hunter none the wiser.

items.lore_text: Every scavenger who walks the gutting floor takes a hook. Most of them are still in here, hanging where they fell.
items.icon_description: A rust-brown steel hook with a frost-white honed tip, wrapped in dark cloth grip, on a black backdrop with a faint amber highlight.

items.name: Scavenger's Sidearm
items.description: A blowback pistol wrapped in felt and oiled rag to choke its report. Pulled from a shallow locker near the entrance, it's the loudest thing you can safely carry — quiet enough to use once, never twice in the same room.

effects.name: Muffled Report
effects.description: The rag wadding halves the shot's carry, but each round still bleeds noise into the room — fire twice and the scavenger has your bearing.

items.lore_text: Found on a scavenger who thought the felt would save him. It muffled the shot; it didn't muffle the boots that came running.
items.icon_description: A stubby dark pistol swaddled in frost-grey rag, amber lamp-glint on the slide, dithered shadow pooling beneath.

items.name: Thawline Scattergun
items.description: A cannery slaughter-gun buried in a sealed cold-crate at the heart of the freezer core. It ends anything in one pull — and the blast rings through all three rooms, ringing the dinner bell for the thing that hunts the loop.

effects.name: Building-Wide Blast
effects.description: A single discharge floods the entire depot with noise, drawing the scavenger straight to your position from wherever it patrols.

items.lore_text: The deepest reward in the Coldstore, and the loudest mistake. The gear that lets you win a fight is the gear that guarantees you have to.
items.icon_description: A wide double-barrel choked with frost, rust bleeding along the receiver, one amber flare of lamplight on the muzzle.

items.name: Insulated Rig Vest
items.description: A quilted dockhand's vest layered with torn thermal blanket. It turns a knife-line into a bruise and keeps the freezer's bite off your ribs long enough to reach the far door.

effects.name: Deadweight Padding
effects.description: The bulk that stops a blade also drags at your stride — sprinting in it is measurably slower.

items.lore_text: Stripped off a body-cache in the freezer core. It kept its last owner warm right up until it didn't keep them quiet.
items.icon_description: A bulky frost-white quilted vest with rust stains at the seams, dithered shadow folds, amber trim on the buckles.

items.name: Feltsole Boots
items.description: Work boots with the treads torn out and thick cannery felt lashed over the soles. On the gutting floor's frost-slick tiles they turn a sprint into a whisper — the single best defense against a hunter that listens for boots.

effects.name: Whispered Stride
effects.description: Even at a full sprint your footfalls generate almost no noise, letting you cover the long walk back without ringing the scavenger's ears.

items.lore_text: The quiet ones last longest in here. The felt was somebody's whole survival plan, and it worked until greed put a loud gun in their hands.
items.icon_description: Scuffed rust-brown boots wrapped in pale grey felt strips, frost caked on the toes, long dithered shadow trailing behind.

items.name: Thermal Syrette
items.description: A one-shot warming stim from a dockworker's first-aid tin. Jabbed into the thigh it dulls the cold-ache and closes a wound fast — but the gasp of relief it pulls out of you carries in the quiet.

effects.name: Warm Surge
effects.description: Restores a chunk of health and clears the freezer's cold-slow for a short window.

items.lore_text: There's always one left in the tin, and always a reason you're bleeding badly enough to want it. The Coldstore is generous with second chances and stingy with thirds.
items.icon_description: A small amber-fluid syrette with a frost-white plunger, red band near the needle, on a dark dithered tile.

items.name: Rattle-Can Decoy
items.description: A dented paint can packed with frozen bolts. Lob it across a room and the clatter yanks the sound-hunting scavenger toward the noise — buying you the seconds to slip a roller door the other way.

effects.name: Throw & Rattle
effects.description: Creates a loud noise source at the landing point that pulls the hunter away from you toward the decoy for its duration.

items.lore_text: The trick every survivor learns and every corpse learned too late: the scavenger chases sound, not sense. Give it something louder than yourself.
items.icon_description: A crushed rust-orange paint can with frost-white bolts spilling from the lid, faint amber rim-light.

items.name: Tin of Door Grease
items.description: Congealed axle grease scraped from the loading dock's dead forklift. Smeared into a roller door's track it silences the groan for a single open — one door you can cross without announcing yourself to the whole building.

effects.name: Silence the Groan
effects.description: The next roller door you open makes no sound, denying the scavenger the announcement it usually gets from a groaning track.

items.lore_text: Three doors, and every one of them a siren. A single tin buys you one quiet threshold — spend it on the door you most need to survive crossing.
items.icon_description: A flat rust-lidded tin half-full of dark amber grease with a bent smearing rag, cold grey highlights.

items.name: Frozen Stock Tin
items.description: A cold-store tin of harbor cannery stock, still sealed and rimed with frost. Worthless as a tool but it fills a rig slot with pure sell-weight — the safe pull for the scavenger who wants to walk out with something for certain.
items.lore_text: The cannery folded with the shelves still full. The stock outlasted the company, the workers, and most of the scavengers who came for it.
items.icon_description: A frost-crusted cylindrical tin with a faded rust-and-amber cannery label, dithered ice glaze across the top.

items.name: Harbor Scrip
items.description: Brass company tokens the cannery paid its dockhands in, now the only currency the scavengers around the Coldstore still trade. What you extract with buys the next run's edge.
items.lore_text: Good only at the harbor, and the harbor's gone. The scavengers kept using it anyway — a dead company's money for a dead man's gear.
items.icon_description: A small stack of tarnished brass tokens stamped with an anchor, frost-white edges, warm amber sheen.

items.name: Ghost-Rig Tags
items.description: A bundle of frozen dog-tags cut from the body-caches in the freezer core — every scavenger who didn't make the dock. Held on your rig, the depot's ghosts read to you: you can feel where the frost claimed a heavy rig into this run's spawns.

effects.name: The Depot Remembers
effects.description: Marks the location of the richest re-seeded body-cache — a prior scavenger's spilled rig — at the start of each run, including one of your own past deaths.

items.lore_text: Everyone who dies in here leaves their rig where they fall, and the frost claims it into the next scavenger's table. Carry the tags and the dead point the way to the dead. One day a stranger will find yours.
items.icon_description: A frozen cluster of stamped steel dog-tags on a wire loop, rime bridging the links, faint amber glow behind the frost.

style_guide.art_style: Tight 32x32px pixel art on a strict integer grid — every sprite, tile, and prop authored at 32x32 native and rendered at integer scale only (3x/4x, nearest-neighbor, no bilinear, no sub-pixel camera). Characters occupy a 16w x 28h silhouette within their 32x32 cell, read-first (recognizable in one flickering frame) with hunched, cold-braced posture. Environment is orthographic top-down-3/4 (2:1 dimetric feel faked in flat tiles) so roller doors, gutting tables, and shelving read as depth without true perspective. Hard 1px outlines are selective, not universal: full dark outline (#1a1418) only where a sprite meets lit floor; outlines DROP to interior shading where a sprite sits in shadow, so figures visually dissolve into the dark exactly like the Listener does. Dithering is the signature technique — 2x2 and 4x4 Bayer checker dithers carry every shadow gradient and every frost-to-rust transition; never use smooth anti-aliased ramps, the grain IS the mood. Palette is hard-capped: max 6 hues + 4 neutral values per sprite. Frost rime is painted as 1-2px stippled highlight clusters on top edges of steel; rust is a dithered mid-brown bleed pooling at bottom edges and weld seams. Loot containers use a shared 32x32 silhouette language with tier-coded lid trim (see palette) so players read value at a glance. Extraction zone is a 2x2 tile stencil of amber hazard-chevrons that pulses. UI is diegetic-minimal: a bottom rig-slot strip (4-6 slots, 24x24 item icons), a 3-segment thin outline map of the loop, and an 8-second extract ring drawn as a depleting 32px arc.
color_palette: #0c0a0d — void black (unlit floor, deep shadow cores, the dark the Listener hides in)
#2b2430 — cold shadow purple-grey (mid shadow, under-table, shelving recesses)
#3d4a52 — steel shadow blue-grey (unlit refrigerated wall/steel base value)
#5b6b70 — cold steel mid (lit fixtures, roller doors, forklift, gutting tables)
#8f9ba0 — frost steel highlight (lit metal edges, chain track, hooks)
#c7d2d4 — rime white (frost stipple, breath fog, ice on shelving — the coldest lit value)
#eef2f0 — frost-white specular (only on directly-lit ice/rime peaks, use sparingly)
#3a2419 — rust shadow brown (deep corrosion, drainage channels, blood-old stains)
#6b4326 — rust brown mid (corroded steel, canvas, wood pallets, Greta's canvas wrap)
#9c6b3d — warm rust / worn leather (rig vests, dock coat, felt-wrapped gear)
#c98a3a — sodium amber mid (the flickering lamp's core glow, extract chevrons)
#f2b64c — sodium amber highlight (lamp filament, hot bloom, extract-zone pulse peak)
#f7d489 — amber specular bloom (1px hot centers only, the filament itself)
#7a2f2f — muted alarm crimson (blood-caches, damage flashes, Listener-alerted vignette tint)
#4a5c4e — sickly frost-green (frozen stock, spoiled body-caches, Kell's ghost glow)
style_guide.mood: Held-breath dread. The screen should feel like standing one room too deep with a full rig — mostly darkness pressed in from the edges, a single trembling pool of amber light you cannot trust, and the constant sense that any bright pixel or loud animation is a mistake that gets you heard. Warmth (amber) means safety and visibility but also exposure; cold (frost-white/steel-blue) means the dark that hides you AND the thing hunting in it. Every visual beat is about the tension between wanting to see and needing to stay unseen. Loot should look tempting and heavy; the walk back should look longer than the walk in. The world visibly accumulates death — spilled rigs, frost-glazed body-caches, and dog-tags dressing the floor so the depot literally shows the wreckage of prior runs.
reference_games: Darkwood — single moving light source, oppressive off-screen darkness, sound-driven dread
Duskers — desaturated industrial-decay palette, cold dread of derelict spaces, minimal diegetic UI
Teleglitch — tight low-res sprites, claustrophobic corridors, grimy top-down survival horror
Hyper Light Drifter — masterclass in limited-palette dithered pixel lighting and silhouette-first readability
Katana ZERO / Death's Door pixel lineage — high-contrast rim-lit sprites against dark grounds (for the light-pool contrast, not the color)
Barotrauma — grim decommissioned-industrial atmosphere, frost/rust materials, threat-in-the-dark tension
Into the Breach — clean 32-ish px tactical readability and tier-coded object silhouettes at small scale
style_guide.line_weight: Selective 1px hard outline. Full #1a1418 outline only where a sprite borders directly-lit floor; outlines thin or vanish into interior shadow where the sprite sits in darkness, letting figures dissolve into the black. Interior detail uses 1px shading lines and dither clusters, never 2px lines — at 32x32 a 2px line eats too much silhouette. Absolutely no outer glow strokes; light bloom is done with palette ramps and dither, not outlines.
style_guide.texture_style: Heavy dithered grime, not clean flats. Every surface carries a material story via 2x2/4x4 Bayer dithering: frost rime stippled along top/lit edges (#c7d2d4 clusters), rust bleeding up from bottoms and weld seams (#6b4326 into #3a2419), and shadow gradients carried entirely by ordered dither rather than smooth ramps. Floors are cold concrete/steel-tile with dithered wear paths and frozen drainage streaks. Grain is intentional and consistent — think 'frost-crusted decommissioned steel,' never smooth or painterly. Keep large flat void areas truly flat (#0c0a0d) so the eye can't parse the dark — that emptiness is a feature.
style_guide.lighting: ONE flickering sodium lamp per room is the entire lighting model — a single warm point source (#f2b64c core → #c98a3a → #9c6b3d falloff → hard dither edge → #0c0a0d void) baked into tiles as a radial dithered gradient. Light is amber and dying; everything outside its pool is near-pure black. FLICKER is the hero animation: an 8-frame looping brightness/position wobble at ~8-10fps, with an irregular timing curve (hold bright 3 frames, stutter-dim 2, near-black 1, recover 2) so it never feels metronomic — the Freezer Core lamp guts to near-#0c0a0d for a full frame between pulses. Every prop with the lamp between it and the wall casts a long hard dithered shadow that SWINGS with the flicker (hooks, shelving, the player) — pre-render 2-3 shadow-angle variants and cross-blend them to the flicker frame so silhouettes physically move. Extract-zone amber chevrons pulse on a separate 6-frame ~4fps breathing cycle. Listener-alerted state washes a subtle #7a2f2f dither vignette in from screen edges (no flashy full-screen flash — keep the dread quiet). Rim-light discipline: cold #8f9ba0/#c7d2d4 edge highlights only on the lamp-facing side of sprites; the far side falls fully to shadow value.

issues.description: The dungeon references loot_table_id 'loot_coldstore_weighted', but no loot table is defined anywhere in the project. Every room lists container entities (loot_crate_common, loot_locker_shallow, loot_body_cache_rare, loot_crate_rare, loot_frozen_stock, loot_crate_uncommon) with no mapping to which item IDs they drop. Because the entire quest chain relies on collecting items out of these containers, no 'collect' objective can be resolved and the game cannot progress past quest_first_walk.
issues.suggested_fix: Author the weighted loot table 'loot_coldstore_weighted' that maps each container entity to a weighted list of concrete item IDs (cs_* items), tiered shallow/mid/deep. Confirm every quest-required item appears in at least one reachable container.

issues.description: Collect objectives mix container-entity IDs with item IDs, so their targets are unresolvable. obj_first_walk_loot collects target 'loot_crate_common' (a container entity, not an item). obj_deep_cache collects target 'loot_body_cache_rare' (container entity). Meanwhile obj_fences_collect collects item 'cs_frozen_stock_tin', but that item is never placed anywhere — only the entity 'loot_frozen_stock' exists in freezer_core. There is no defined path from that entity to the tin, so 'The Fence's Cut' cannot be completed.
issues.suggested_fix: Standardize collect targets to item IDs, and make containers drop those items via the loot table. Explicitly have loot_frozen_stock yield cs_frozen_stock_tin so the 3-tin objective is satisfiable.

issues.description: stat_system is null and combat_system is null, yet the design depends on both. Items declare stat_modifiers (melee_damage, ranged_damage, armor, stealth, noise, aim_stability, cold_resistance, carry_slots, move_speed) with no stat system to consume them. The player has no defined HP, so The Listener's attack of 28 and the 120-HP boss fight in quest_silence_the_listener cannot be resolved. Rig 'limited-slot' is central to the loop but the slot count is never given numerically (style_guide vaguely says '4-6 slots'; cs_thawline_scattergun uses carry_slots -1 against an undefined total).
issues.location: stat_system: null; combat_system: null; world.global_properties.rig; items[2].stat_modifiers (carry_slots)
issues.suggested_fix: Define a minimal stat system (player HP, noise meter, exact rig slot count) and a combat resolution model (damage vs defense, noise generation on attack) so item modifiers and the boss fight have something to act on.

issues.description: Several quests place the quest at a room the quest-giver can never physically reach, given the NPCs' own established constraints. quest_run_silent is given by Greta but has location_id 'loading_dock' — Greta's schedule is 'always' at gutting_floor and her whole character is that she never passes the first door. quest_deep_pull and quest_silence_the_listener are given by Marrow but have location_id 'freezer_core' — Marrow's defining rule is she 'never crosses the extraction line inward' and stays at the bay door. As written, the player cannot receive/turn in these quests where they are anchored.
issues.location: quests[2] (Run Silent), quests[3] (The Deep Pull), quests[5] (Silence the Listener)
issues.suggested_fix: Set each quest's location_id to the giver's actual room (gutting_floor for Greta, loading_dock for Marrow), and frame the objectives as taking place elsewhere. Handoff/turn-in should occur where the NPC stands.

issues.description: The USP promises exactly ONE sound-hunting hunter ('A single sound-hunting AI scavenger'), but the rooms each list a different enemy entity ID — enemy_scavenger_patrol (gutting_floor), enemy_scavenger (freezer_core), enemy_scavenger_lure (loading_dock) — in addition to the boss npc_the_listener. It is ambiguous whether these are one roaming entity or three separate spawns, which directly contradicts the single-hunter design pillar if instantiated literally.
issues.suggested_fix: Represent the hunter as one persistent entity that patrols the loop (npc_the_listener), and remove the per-room enemy_scavenger_* placeholders or clearly mark them as spawn hints for the same single actor.

issues.description: level_requirement gates exist (quest_deep_pull=2, quest_depot_remembers=2, quest_silence_the_listener=3) and quests award XP (100/80/150/220/260/500), but with no stat_system there is no leveling curve, XP-to-level thresholds, or persistence model across permadeath runs. There is no defined way for the player to actually reach level 2 or 3, so the gated quests may be permanently locked.
issues.suggested_fix: Define XP thresholds and where levels persist (per-run vs meta-progression that survives death). Confirm the early quests grant enough XP to clear the level-2/3 gates before those quests unlock.

issues.description: The unique key item cs_ghost_rig_tags (epic, stackable:false, max_stack:1) is duplicated and given circularly. It is in npc_frostbit_kell.inventory AND npc_the_listener.inventory, and quest_depot_remembers both COLLECTS it (obj_remember_tags) and awards it again as a reward item — the player receives the same unique item they were required to already hold.
issues.suggested_fix: Give quest_depot_remembers a distinct reward (e.g., the recovered ghost-rig loot or scrip), remove cs_ghost_rig_tags from The Listener's inventory, and treat Kell as the single source of the tags.

issues.description: npc_the_listener is is_essential: true, yet quest_silence_the_listener requires killing it (objective_type 'kill', count 1). An essential flag typically prevents death; the two states contradict. If a build honors is_essential, the required boss kill becomes impossible.
issues.suggested_fix: Set is_essential: false for The Listener, or add a scripted despawn/defeat state so the kill objective can complete while preserving it for runs where the player never triggers the fight.

issues.description: Quest rewards use a generic 'gold' field (40/70/60/130/90/300) but the world's only currency is cs_harbor_scrip (brass scrip). The terminology mismatch could cause the reward payout to reference a currency that doesn't exist in-game.
issues.suggested_fix: Map the 'gold' reward field to Harbor Scrip explicitly, or rename to keep the fiction consistent.

issues.description: obj_remember_find uses objective_type 'explore' with target 'loot_body_cache_rare' — an 'explore' objective is pointed at a loot container rather than a location/zone. This type/target mismatch may not resolve in an explore-tracking system that expects a room or POI.
issues.suggested_fix: Change the type to 'reach'/'interact' against the seeded cache, or point 'explore' at the freezer_core room and have the tags reveal the cache location.

warnings: estimated_playtime_hours is 6.0 while target_run_seconds is 300 (~72 runs). The meta-progression that would fill 6 hours (persistent scrip, gear carry-over, quest chain length) is not fully specified — the six quests alone will not sustain that runtime.

Permadeath spills the whole rig on death, but delivery quests (quest_fences_cut needs 3 tins delivered; quest_deep_pull needs the rare pull extracted) require carrying items out alive. This is intentional tension, but there is no partial-credit or per-run persistence defined, so these quests may feel punishingly RNG-dependent across many failed runs.

No player starting loadout/inventory is defined. quest_run_silent forbids firing the Sidearm/Scattergun and implies a silent option (Gutting Hook, decoys, door grease), but nothing guarantees the player starts with or can reliably find a silent weapon.

The extract chime draws the hunter for 8 seconds every extraction, which is also the failure condition for quest_first_walk (die before extraction). New players with no gear may find the very first tutorial extraction disproportionately lethal without a guaranteed safe window.
encounters, scenes_generated, and scripts_generated are all empty — this is a design spec only; none of the above systems have been implemented yet, so 'playable' cannot be verified against a build.
suggestions: Author the missing loot table with explicit entity→item drop weights, tiered by room depth, and unit-test that every quest-required item (cs_frozen_stock_tin, the rare body-cache contents, cs_thawline_scattergun) is reachable.
Add a compact stat_system: player HP, a 0–100 noise meter the hunter reacts to, and an exact rig slot count (pick a number, e.g. 5, and reconcile cs_thawline_scattergun's carry_slots:-1 against it).

Add a combat_system defining damage vs defense and per-weapon noise, so the Sidearm (noise 45/2 rooms), Scattergun (noise 100/3 rooms, draws hunter), and the 120-HP Listener fight all resolve consistently.
Fix quest anchoring: set location_id to the giver's real room and describe far-room objectives in text (Greta briefs at the gutting floor, Marrow at the bay door).
Consolidate the hunter into a single persistent patrolling entity to honor the one-hunter USP, removing the three per-room enemy_scavenger_* placeholders.
Deduplicate the ghost-rig tags (single source: Kell) and give quest_depot_remembers a non-circular reward.
Define the cross-run meta-progression (persistent scrip bank at Marrow, unlockable starting gear) that justifies the 6-hour playtime and gives the level_requirement gates a way to be met.
qa_report.summary: Coldstore is an exceptionally cohesive and atmospheric design — the three-room extraction loop, sound-hunting Listener, noise/greed tension, and permadeath re-seeding all reinforce each other, and the NPC/item/lore layer is tight and evocative. However, it is not yet playable as specified. Two blockers stop progression: (1) the referenced loot table 'loot_coldstore_weighted' is undefined and containers have no drop mapping, and (2) collect objectives mix container-entity IDs with item IDs (notably cs_frozen_stock_tin is never actually spawnable), making core quests uncompletable. Major gaps compound this: stat_system and combat_system are both null despite items, a 120-HP boss kill, level gates (2/3), and rig slot mechanics all depending on them; and three quests are anchored to rooms their givers can never reach. Fix the loot/data integrity, define the missing stat/combat systems and rig slot count, and reconcile quest-giver locations, then re-run QA against an actual build. Strong foundation, blocked on implementation-level definitions. Exporter note: this build now includes generated scene/script files; remaining QA issues should be read as the next layer of specificity, not as a blank-template failure.
